An economist records data on the volume of corn exports $y$ (in thousands of tons) from the United States to a particular country, $x$ number of years since $2010.$
The residual plot above was constructed after fitting a linear regression model on this data set. Which of the following statements are true?

I. When $t=6,$ the regression equation underestimates the value of $y.$

II. The residuals appear randomly scattered about the horizontal axis (there are no obvious trends).

III. This linear regression is probably a good fit for the data.

The residual plot above was constructed after fitting a linear regression model on a set of bivariate numerical data $(x,y).$
Which of the following statements are true?

I. When $x=4,$ the regression equation underestimates the value of $y.$

II. The residuals appear to be randomly scattered about the horizontal axis (there are no obvious trends).

III. This linear regression is probably a good fit for the data.
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's examine the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. The residual equals the actual value minus the estimated value:

$$
\textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated}
$$

 
From the plot, the residual at $x=4$ is positive. So, we have that $\text{Actual} >     \textrm{Estimated},$ and therefore the model underestimates  this data point.

- Statement II is false. The plot shows the residuals tend to decrease as $x$ increases. So, there is a trend, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/b02727029ed43c985da639287afa452cbe1985dc2bae8eaa4f16452ac4c01518.png)

   

- Statement III is false. Since the residuals are *not* randomly scattered above and below the horizontal axis, our regression line is *not* a good fit for the given data.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
